episode.title: Is it intent or impact that matters in our relationships?

candidates.speaker: Spencer Greenberg
candidates.text: I actually have a term I call "light gassing" for when someone reinforces your false perceptions, so it's the opposite of gaslighting.

candidates.speaker: Spencer Greenberg
candidates.text: Sometimes we want there to be this dichotomy: either you're a victim and there's nothing you can do, or you're not a victim. But actually, you can be a victim, and also there's something you can do, and actually there's something you really should do just for your own benefit.

candidates.speaker: Spencer Greenberg
candidates.text: I don't think blame as a concept really does anything in scenarios where nobody's taking responsibility.

candidates.speaker: Shawni Turner
candidates.text: I would almost argue that likability or dislikeability in friendships is not important. It's just information. It's just a data point.

candidates.speaker: Shawni Turner
candidates.text: What am I treating as obviously true because I've stopped noticing the assumptions underneath it?

candidates.speaker: Spencer Greenberg
candidates.text: You need a deep mental model of what's really going on sometimes to solve things, and if you pattern match, you can end up with a completely backward solution.

candidates.speaker: Spencer Greenberg
candidates.text: If someone could not have predicted your reaction, I don't see how we could hold them responsible for it.

candidates.speaker: Shawni Turner
candidates.text: I think it gets really interesting when we start to assign this therapy speak to these interactions because we're potentially pathologizing very ordinary relationship dynamics, interpersonal dynamics that are happening.

candidates.speaker: Shawni Turner
candidates.text: At the end of the day, it doesn't matter what the label is on the behavior. If it's not something I'm willing to be a part of, I have the opportunity and the autonomy to leave that situation.

candidates.speaker: Spencer Greenberg
candidates.text: I find that often what people want to bring to those conversations when someone else is in need is what they would want in the same scenario.

highlight: you can be a victim, and also there's something you can do
note: Vote winner A (light gassing) was rejected by Igor on 2026-11-20; he chose the runner-up B.
